content.summary:
**Analysis and Code Generation for Contact Card UI**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. The core requirement is a UI card for contact information. The root must be a `Card`, identified by `id="root"`. This card needs to hold a `Row`, and then a button below the row, so the initial thought is that we need a vertical layout container: a `Column`, to hold both. Inside this card, let's create a `Column`. Inside the column, a `Row` will contain the avatar `Image` and a second `Column` for the contact details: name, email, and phone, each rendered as `Text` components. Below this main `Row`, the `Column` must contain a `Button` labeled "View on Map," also using a `Text` child.

Now, let's enforce all the rules! We are going to use the `ui-` prefix in kebab-case. We need unique `id` attributes and, per the guidance, we will "nest child components directly inside parent tags." The initial thinking about `child` attributes is wrong. Don't use a child attribute! The instructions say "Do NOT pass layout properties (like `children` or `child`) as attributes." The correct structure is standard HTML nesting: `<ui-card><ui-column><ui-row><ui-image /><ui-column><ui-text /><ui-text /><ui-text /></ui-column></ui-row><ui-button><ui-text /></ui-button></ui-column></ui-card>`.

We'll use a placeholder URL for the avatar. The "View on Map" button will trigger an `openUrl` function with a Google Maps link. The `on-click` is an inline expression and we will need to use curly braces for the attribute.

Let's double-check the `Button`'s need for a nested `Text` component. Yes, a Button needs a child `Text`. We are nesting the components directly.

Static strings for name, email, phone, and button label are fine without a data block or data initialization.

Let's review the final structure:
`Card` > `Column` > `Row` > `Image`, `Column` > `Text`, `Text`, `Text` and then the `Column` also holds `Button` > `Text`. We are following all instructions precisely: static string attributes, no child attributes, no data block, on-click with curly braces for expressions, named arguments, and nesting children. The final HTML is the following:
```html
<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <ui-card id="root">
      <ui-column id="mainLayout" align="stretch" justify="start">
        <ui-row id="contactRow" align="center" justify="start">
          <ui-image id="avatar" url="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1494790108377-be9c29b29330?auto=format&fit=crop&w=150&h=150" variant="avatar" description="Avatar of Jane Doe" />
          <ui-column id="detailsColumn" align="start">
            <ui-text id="nameText" text="Jane Doe" />
            <ui-text id="emailText" text="jane.doe@example.com" variant="caption" />
            <ui-text id="phoneText" text="(123) 456-7890" variant="caption" />
          </ui-column>
        </ui-row>
        <ui-divider id="divider" axis="horizontal" />
        <ui-button id="mapButton" variant="primary" on-click="{openUrl(url: 'https://maps.google.com/?q=Jane+Doe')}">
          <ui-text id="buttonText" text="View on Map" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-column>
    </ui-card>
  </body>
</a2ui>
```

Let's do a quick validation of rule 3: attributes with static strings (no braces), expressions are wrapped in double-quoted curly braces. Rule 6 is also verified (named arguments). Rule 9, actions with inline expressions using `on-click`. All looks good. Ready to go.

Given the criteria and the submission, it appears to be completely correct.

I'll make sure there's one root component with the ID "root." Based on the requirements and my experience, a vertical column seems like the most logical starting point for the form's overall layout.

Next, I need to focus on how child components are nested and laid out. A critical constraint is the nesting of child components; it seems like I *must* nest them directly inside their parent tags, and *not* rely on attributes like `children` or `child`, unless we're dealing with named slots. I recall reading about this specifically regarding layout elements like `<ui-column>` and `<ui-row>`. I've also re-read the documentation and examples. The examples are really clear: nesting child elements directly is the correct approach. Named slots are where we use the `slot` attribute. For example, a button's label should be nested using `<ui-text slot="child" ...>`. I'm absolutely clear on this now.

So, the form will include a title ("# New Event," using markdown for the heading), an "Event Title" text field, a row for start and end time (using `ui-date-time-input`), a checkbox for "All-day event," and a row with "Save" and "Cancel" buttons. The *key* part is how these are rendered and nested.

*   The title will be a `<ui-text>` component with the text "# New Event".
*   The "Event Title" will be a `<ui-text-field>`, binding to the data path `$/event/title` for its value.
*   The two date-time inputs ("Start Time" and "End Time") will be in a `<ui-row>`. Importantly, the instructions state "initialize both with a literal empty string value: ''" and not bind to a data path. It's best to use `value=""`. I will set `enable-date` and `enable-time` to "{true}" as they are booleans, and double checked the data types. I'll use `weight` to distribute space inside the row.
*   The "All-day event" checkbox will be a `<ui-check-box>`, bound to `$/event/allDay`.
*   The "Save" and "Cancel" buttons will also be in a `<ui-row>`. The `save` button will use the primary variant.
*   The buttons will use named slots, so I'll nest `<ui-text slot="child" ...>` inside each `<ui-button>`.

I'll keep data bindings as clean and as standard as possible. I'll also ensure all actions are defined using `on-click="{Event('...')}"` attributes. I'll need a script to define the data model for bindings, and I'll keep it at the top level of the body element.

Finally, I'll review *every* single detail against all constraints. I'll also double-check my attribute formatting (e.g. `enable-date="{true}"` for boolean values, static strings without curly braces, and correct use of the `slot` attribute) and ensure the overall structure is logically sound. I will make sure all components use the `ui-` prefix and are properly closed, and that the markup is valid XML.

<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "event": {
          "title": "",
          "allDay": false
        }
      }
    </script>

    <ui-column id="root" align="stretch" justify="start">
      <ui-text id="headerText" text="# New Event" />
      
      <ui-text-field id="eventTitle" label="Event Title" value="{$/event/title}" placeholder="Enter event title" />
      
      <ui-row id="dateTimeRow" justify="spaceBetween">
        <ui-date-time-input id="startTime" label="Start Time" value="" enable-date="{true}" enable-time="{true}" weight="{1}" />
        <ui-date-time-input id="endTime" label="End Time" value="" enable-date="{true}" enable-time="{true}" weight="{1}" />
      </ui-row>
      
      <ui-check-box id="allDay" label="All-day event" value="{$/event/allDay}" />
      
      <ui-row id="buttonRow" justify="end">
        <ui-button id="cancelBtn" on-click="{Event('cancel_event')}">
          <ui-text slot="child" id="cancelBtnText" text="Cancel" />
        </ui-button>
        <ui-button id="saveBtn" on-click="{Event('save_event')}" variant="primary">
          <ui-text slot="child" id="saveBtnText" text="Save" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

**UI Design Deep Dive: A Social Media Post Component**

Okay, here's how I'm approaching this UI task. First, I analyzed the request: the goal is a social media post component with a 'main' surface, and a `Card` as the root with id 'root'. It contains a `Column`, which in turn, holds a series of components: a user info row with an avatar and username; the post content text; the post image; and an actions row with like, comment, and share buttons. That's the basic structure.

Now, let's make sure that the building blocks comply with the A2UI spec. The `Card` component interface is clear: it needs a *single* child. However, the documentation stresses that I should *not* define the child inline or use the `child` attribute (which seems contradictory at first, but Example 2 is nested correctly). Rule 7 is king, so I'll nest the `Column` inside the `Card`. It's straightforward: no `child` attribute.

I then move on to the `Button`. Its interface also presents this `child` property. But again, Rule 7 prevails! I'll nest a `Text` component directly inside the `Button`, as seen in Example 1. No attributes like `children` or `child`. Just good old nesting.

With this knowledge in hand, I sketched the basic HTML structure. I start with the root: a `<ui-card id="root">`, containing a `<ui-column id="postContainer">`. Inside this column, I define the nested components: the header row with the avatar and username, the post content text, the post image, and the actions row with the buttons.

Now, let's refine the details. The root element must have the `id="root"`. I need unique `id`s for every component. That's a must. And, no mixing positional arguments and named arguments, that's not needed here since we are just nesting. I need to make sure I am following the A2UI Elemental format. I've also double-checked the catalog import and how to correctly use event expressions: `on-click="{Event('like')}"`. The code is using this correctly. I am going to keep static attributes as permitted: "Pass static strings as regular attributes without curly braces."

Let's double-check the rules: all components tags are prefixed with `ui-`, all are unique `id`s. I should wrap numbers, booleans, and expressions in curly braces.

I reviewed the available A2UI values for various component attributes, such as `variant` on `ui-image` (`avatar` is good) and `align` on `ui-row` (`center` is valid). The `justify` property on `ui-row` is a bit interesting: I'll use `"spaceEvenly"` or `"space-around"` and I'll keep the value exactly as defined (as opposed to kebab-casing it).

Finally, I double-checked the data structure, all components are uniquely identified. All components and constraints are now satisfied, and the data structures align with the A2UI spec.

It contains a `Column`, which in turn, holds a series of components: a user info row with an avatar and username; the post content text; the post image; and an actions row with like, comment, and share buttons. That's the basic structure.

Now, let's make sure that the building blocks comply with the A2UI spec. The `Card` component interface is clear: it needs a *single* child. However, the documentation stresses that I should *not* define the child inline or use the `child` attribute (which seems contradictory at first, but Example 2 is nested correctly). Rule 7 is king, so I'll nest the `Column` inside the `Card`. It's straightforward: no `child` attribute.

I then move on to the `Button`. Its interface also presents this `child` property. But again, Rule 7 prevails! I'll nest a `Text` component directly inside the `Button`, as seen in Example 1. No attributes like `children` or `child`. Just good old nesting.

With this knowledge in hand, I sketched the basic HTML structure. I start with the root: a `<ui-card id="root">`, containing a `<ui-column id="postContainer">`. Inside this column, I define the nested components: the header row with the avatar and username, the post content text, the post image, and the actions row with the buttons.

Now, let's refine the details. The root element must have the `id="root"`. I need unique `id`s for every component. That's a must. And, no mixing positional arguments and named arguments, that's not needed here since we are just nesting. I need to make sure I am following the A2UI Elemental format. I've also double-checked the catalog import and how to correctly use event expressions: `on-click="{Event('like')}"`. The code is using this correctly. I am going to keep static attributes as permitted: "Pass static strings as regular attributes without curly braces."

Let's double-check the rules: all components tags are prefixed with `ui-`, all are unique `id`s. I should wrap numbers, booleans, and expressions in curly braces.

I reviewed the available A2UI values for various component attributes, such as `variant` on `ui-image` (`avatar` is good) and `align` on `ui-row` (`center` is valid). The `justify` property on `ui-row` is a bit interesting: I'll use `"spaceEvenly"` or `"space-around"` and I'll keep the value exactly as defined (as opposed to kebab-casing it).

Finally, I double-checked the data structure, all components are uniquely identified. All components and constraints are now satisfied, and the data structures align with the A2UI spec.

Alright, let's break this down systematically. The core task is to render a UI for a product listing within the A2UI framework. My approach starts with a careful dissection of the requirements and then meticulously translating them into the correct component hierarchy and A2UI syntax.

First, I established the fundamental structure. The surface ID is 'main', and the root element is a `ui-row` with `id="root"`. This `Row` is the top-level container, horizontally dividing the layout into two columns: one for product images and another for details and actions.

The left column contains the product images. It will consist of a main, large image displayed via `ui-image` and then a `ui-row` holding three smaller thumbnail images, also using `ui-image`. For this main image, and the thumbnails, I need image URLs. I'll define these within a data block. I will define a static image, or mock it with an image URL. Binding these data values later ensures proper dynamic rendering. I'll specify variant as `"largeFeature"` for the main image and `"smallFeature"` for the thumbnails to control the style and rendering.

On the right side of the root row, I'll place the product information. This includes a text label for the product name (which I will keep as "# Premium Leather Jacket" as specified), the price text, a `ui-divider`, and then a `ui-choice-picker` for selecting size. The choice picker must have mutually exclusive options, so its variant will be `"mutuallyExclusive"`. I'll do the same for selecting the color. Each of these requires options and bindings. All options will be defined within the script tags, as is dictated by the A2UI rules, and the `value` will be bound to arrays or strings (likely strings in this case).

After those pickers, there's a button. This is a `ui-button` component that triggers an "add_to_cart" event on click. Its text content will be "Add to Cart", which requires a nested `ui-text` child defined within a slot. Finally, I'll add a text component for the product description.

Following this, I ensured the structure conforms to the A2UI requirements. I had to pay close attention to the component nesting and avoiding layout properties as attributes. The rule to nest children elements directly inside the parent tags is very explicit.

Data initialization is handled with a `<script type="application/json">` block. Within, I define the initial state, setting values for `selectedSize` and `selectedColor`. I will also define the product data, including the name, price, description, and URLs for the images (main and thumbnails). Image URLs are placeholder and could be static if the data is not dynamic.

*   For the button, I used `on-click="{Event('add_to_cart')}"` as defined in the A2UI spec.
*   Components use named slots and nested components correctly: `<ui-text slot="child" id="btnText" text="Add to Cart" />`.

I also cross-referenced these considerations with the TypeScript definitions for each component to double-check parameters and property usage.

Finally, I made some refinements. I used `weight="{1}"` on both left and right columns within the root row so that the UI can be responsive to different screen sizes. I ensured all elements are direct descendants to the column.

*   Components are nested according to the specifications.

Create a UI on surface 'main' for a product details page.
The main layout should be a 'Row'.
The left side of the row is a 'Column' containing a large main 'Image' of the product, and below it, a 'Row' of three smaller thumbnail 'Image' components.
The right side of the row is another 'Column' for product information:
- A 'Text'  for the product name, "# Premium Leather Jacket".
- A 'Text' component for the price, "$299.99".
- A 'Divider'.
- A 'ChoicePicker' (variant 'mutuallyExclusive') labeled "Select Size" with options "S", "M", "L", "XL".
- A 'ChoicePicker' (variant 'mutuallyExclusive') labeled "Select Color" with options "Black", "Brown", "Red".
- A 'Button' with a 'Text' child "Add to Cart".
- A 'Text' component for the product description below the button.

content.summary:
**Finalized UI Construction Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. The core task is to render a UI for a product listing within the A2UI framework. My approach starts with a careful dissection of the requirements and then meticulously translating them into the correct component hierarchy and A2UI syntax.

First, I established the fundamental structure. The surface ID is 'main', and the root element is a `ui-row` with `id="root"`. This `Row` is the top-level container, horizontally dividing the layout into two columns: one for product images and another for details and actions.

The left column contains the product images. It will consist of a main, large image displayed via `ui-image` and then a `ui-row` holding three smaller thumbnail images, also using `ui-image`. For this main image, and the thumbnails, I need image URLs. I'll define these within a data block. I will define a static image, or mock it with an image URL. Binding these data values later ensures proper dynamic rendering. I'll specify variant as `"largeFeature"` for the main image and `"smallFeature"` for the thumbnails to control the style and rendering.

On the right side of the root row, I'll place the product information. This includes a text label for the product name (which I will keep as "# Premium Leather Jacket" as specified), the price text, a `ui-divider`, and then a `ui-choice-picker` for selecting size. The choice picker must have mutually exclusive options, so its variant will be `"mutuallyExclusive"`. I'll do the same for selecting the color. Each of these requires options and bindings. All options will be defined within the script tags, as is dictated by the A2UI rules, and the `value` will be bound to arrays or strings (likely strings in this case).

After those pickers, there's a button. This is a `ui-button` component that triggers an "add_to_cart" event on click. Its text content will be "Add to Cart", which requires a nested `ui-text` child defined within a slot. Finally, I'll add a text component for the product description.

Following this, I ensured the structure conforms to the A2UI requirements. I had to pay close attention to the component nesting and avoiding layout properties as attributes. The rule to nest children elements directly inside the parent tags is very explicit.

Data initialization is handled with a `<script type="application/json">` block. Within, I define the initial state, setting values for `selectedSize` and `selectedColor`. I will also define the product data, including the name, price, description, and URLs for the images (main and thumbnails). Image URLs are placeholder and could be static if the data is not dynamic.

Syntax and formatting rules were meticulously adhered to:
*   `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` are the outermost wrappers.
*   The `<body>` has the `id="main"`.
*   The basic catalog link is included.
*   Curly braces used for binding: for example, `weight="{1}"` or `url="{$/product/mainImageUrl}"`.
*   For the button, I used `on-click="{Event('add_to_cart')}"` as defined in the A2UI spec.
*   Components use named slots and nested components correctly: `<ui-text slot="child" id="btnText" text="Add to Cart" />`.

I also cross-referenced these considerations with the TypeScript definitions for each component to double-check parameters and property usage.

Finally, I made some refinements. I used `weight="{1}"` on both left and right columns within the root row so that the UI can be responsive to different screen sizes. I ensured all elements are direct descendants to the column.

After writing the code block, I double-checked the following:
*   Layout is correct, as specified by the prompt.
*   Syntax matches the A2UI rules.
*   Correct use of binding to dynamic data or static values.
*   Components are nested according to the specifications.

The result is a fully compliant and structurally sound A2UI rendering of the requested UI.

<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "selectedSize": [],
        "selectedColor": [],
        "product": {
          "name": "# Premium Leather Jacket",
          "price": "$299.99",
          "description": "Crafted from top-grade genuine leather, this premium jacket offers a classic silhouette with modern durability. Features robust silver-tone hardware, multiple utility pockets, and a soft interior lining designed for ultimate comfort and seasonal versatility.",
          "mainImageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551028719-00167b16eac5?w=800&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb1Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551028719-00167b16eac5?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb2Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1521223890158-f9f7c3d5d504?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb3Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1481949181371-97a92af30b4b?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80"
        }
      }
    </script>
    
    <ui-row id="root" justify="spaceEvenly" align="start">
      <!-- Left side of the row: Column containing main image and thumbnails -->
      <ui-column id="leftImageColumn" weight="{1}" align="stretch">
        <ui-image id="mainProductImage" url="{$/product/mainImageUrl}" description="Main Product Preview" variant="largeFeature" fit="cover" />
        <ui-row id="thumbnailRow" justify="spaceBetween" align="center">
          <ui-image id="thumb1" url="{$/product/thumb1Url}" description="Product Thumb 1" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
          <ui-image id="thumb2" url="{$/product/thumb2Url}" description="Product Thumb 2" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
          <ui-image id="thumb3" url="{$/product/thumb3Url}" description="Product Thumb 3" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
        </ui-row>
      </ui-column>

      <!-- Right side of the row: Column containing product information -->
      <ui-column id="rightInfoColumn" weight="{1}" align="stretch">
        <ui-text id="productName" text="{$/product/name}" />
        <ui-text id="productPrice" text="{$/product/price}" />
        <ui-divider id="detailsDivider" axis="horizontal" />
        
        <ui-choice-picker id="sizePicker" label="Select Size" variant="mutuallyExclusive" value="{$/selectedSize}">
          <script type="application/json" slot="options">
            [
              {"label": "S", "value": "S"},
              {"label": "M", "value": "M"},
              {"label": "L", "value": "L"},
              {"label": "XL", "value": "XL"}
            ]
          </script>
        </ui-choice-picker>

        <ui-choice-picker id="colorPicker" label="Select Color" variant="mutuallyExclusive" value="{$/selectedColor}">
          <script type="application/json" slot="options">
            [
              {"label": "Black", "value": "Black"},
              {"label": "Brown", "value": "Brown"},
              {"label": "Red", "value": "Red"}
            ]
          </script>
        </ui-choice-picker>

        <ui-button id="addToCartButton" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('add_to_cart')}">
          <ui-text slot="child" id="buttonText" text="Add to Cart" />
        </ui-button>

        <ui-text id="productDescription" text="{$/product/description}" />
      </ui-column>
    </ui-row>
  </body>
</a2ui>

  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "selectedSize": [],
        "selectedColor": [],
        "product": {
          "name": "# Premium Leather Jacket",
          "price": "$299.99",
          "description": "Crafted from top-grade genuine leather, this premium jacket offers a classic silhouette with modern durability. Features robust silver-tone hardware, multiple utility pockets, and a soft interior lining designed for ultimate comfort and seasonal versatility.",
          "mainImageUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551028719-00167b16eac5?w=800&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb1Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551028719-00167b16eac5?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb2Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1521223890158-f9f7c3d5d504?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80",
          "thumb3Url": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1481949181371-97a92af30b4b?w=150&auto=format&fit=crop&q=80"
        }
      }
    </script>
    
    <ui-row id="root" justify="spaceEvenly" align="start">
      <!-- Left side of the row: Column containing main image and thumbnails -->
      <ui-column id="leftImageColumn" weight="{1}" align="stretch">
        <ui-image id="mainProductImage" url="{$/product/mainImageUrl}" description="Main Product Preview" variant="largeFeature" fit="cover" />
        <ui-row id="thumbnailRow" justify="spaceBetween" align="center">
          <ui-image id="thumb1" url="{$/product/thumb1Url}" description="Product Thumb 1" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
          <ui-image id="thumb2" url="{$/product/thumb2Url}" description="Product Thumb 2" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
          <ui-image id="thumb3" url="{$/product/thumb3Url}" description="Product Thumb 3" variant="smallFeature" fit="cover" weight="{1}" />
        </ui-row>
      </ui-column>

      <!-- Right side of the row: Column containing product information -->
      <ui-column id="rightInfoColumn" weight="{1}" align="stretch">
        <ui-text id="productName" text="{$/product/name}" />
        <ui-text id="productPrice" text="{$/product/price}" />
        <ui-divider id="detailsDivider" axis="horizontal" />
        
        <ui-choice-picker id="sizePicker" label="Select Size" variant="mutuallyExclusive" value="{$/selectedSize}">
          <script type="application/json" slot="options">
            [
              {"label": "S", "value": "S"},
              {"label": "M", "value": "M"},
              {"label": "L", "value": "L"},
              {"label": "XL", "value": "XL"}
            ]
          </script>
        </ui-choice-picker>

        <ui-choice-picker id="colorPicker" label="Select Color" variant="mutuallyExclusive" value="{$/selectedColor}">
          <script type="application/json" slot="options">
            [
              {"label": "Black", "value": "Black"},
              {"label": "Brown", "value": "Brown"},
              {"label": "Red", "value": "Red"}
            ]
          </script>
        </ui-choice-picker>

        <ui-button id="addToCartButton" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('add_to_cart')}">
          <ui-text slot="child" id="buttonText" text="Add to Cart" />
        </ui-button>

        <ui-text id="productDescription" text="{$/product/description}" />
      </ui-column>
    </ui-row>
  </body>
</a2ui>

**Interactive Dashboard UI Creation - My Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down. My objective is crystal clear: build an interactive analytics dashboard UI using A2UI's Elemental HTML5-like markup on the 'main' surface. I'm leveraging my understanding of the A2UI framework.

First, I've confirmed that the top-level container needs `id="main"` on the `<body>` tag, adhering to Rule 1. Now, onto the components. The core structure will be a vertical column (`<ui-column>`) with `id="root"`—that's the root container. Inside, I’ll add a text heading, a filter section with date inputs and an apply button. Then two metrics cards in a row. Finally a card with a chart. I'll need a way to initialize those date values.

Data initialization is handled with a JSON script. I'll be initializing `startDate` and `endDate` to empty strings within the data model. This allows for clean handling of the filter data. The data model is:
```json
{
  "filters": {
    "startDate": "",
    "endDate": ""
  }
}
```

The component tree will have me nest child components directly inside the parent tags, not as attributes as per Rule 7. I'll be using kebab-case for the element names. I'm using TypeScript, which has defined an HTML schema that I’ll be adhering to. Let's start sketching that out.
```html
<ui-column id="root">
   <ui-text id="titleText" text="# Company Dashboard" />
   <ui-card id="filtersCard">
      <ui-row id="filtersRow">
        <ui-date-time-input id="startDateInput" label="Start Date" value="{$/filters/startDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-date-time-input id="endDateInput" label="End Date" value="{$/filters/endDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-button id="applyBtn" on-click="{Event('apply_filters')}">
          <ui-text id="applyBtnText" text="Apply Filters" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>
   </ui-card>
   <ui-row id="metricsRow">
      <ui-card id="revenueCard" weight="{1}">
         <ui-column id="revenueCol">
            <ui-text id="revenueTitle" text="## Total Revenue" />
            <ui-text id="revenueValue" text="$1,234,567" />
         </ui-column>
      </ui-card>
      <ui-card id="usersCard" weight="{1}">
         <ui-column id="usersCol">
            <ui-text id="usersTitle" text="## New Users" />
            <ui-text id="usersValue" text="4,321" />
         </ui-column>
      </ui-card>
   </ui-row>
   <ui-card id="chartCard">
      <ui-column id="chartCol">
         <ui-text id="chartTitle" text="## Revenue Over Time" />
         <ui-image id="chartImage" url="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551288049-bebda4e38f71?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=80" description="Line chart showing revenue over time" />
      </ui-column>
   </ui-card>
</ui-column>
```
Rule 7 is key here. It prevents a lot of layout misconfigurations that can happen when developers have an existing knowledge of React or Angular.

Now, let's double-check the components against HTML5 best practices and the A2UI rules. Prefixing all tags with `ui-`, unique `id`s, putting everything inside the parent tags (not as attributes), are crucial. All expressions are correctly wrapped in `{` and `}`, and data paths follow `{$/path}` format. For the `<ui-button>` I'll be using `on-click` to respond to the click event correctly, as the TypeScript definitions support an action to be used as an attribute.

I have double checked the attribute formatting and have ensured the HTML is now well-formed.

The image component will use a placeholder chart, like a screenshot of a line chart from an open resource. No need to overcomplicate the visual at this stage.

Finally, the code blocks will go inside a root `<body>`

**Interactive Dashboard UI Creation - My Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down. My objective is crystal clear: build an interactive analytics dashboard UI using A2UI's Elemental HTML5-like markup on the 'main' surface. I'm leveraging my understanding of the A2UI framework.

First, I've confirmed that the top-level container needs `id="main"` on the `<body>` tag, adhering to Rule 1. Now, onto the components. The core structure will be a vertical column (`<ui-column>`) with `id="root"`—that's the root container. Inside, I’ll add a text heading, a filter section with date inputs and an apply button. Then two metrics cards in a row. Finally a card with a chart. I'll need a way to initialize those date values.

Data initialization is handled with a JSON script. I'll be initializing `startDate` and `endDate` to empty strings within the data model. This allows for clean handling of the filter data. The data model is:
```json
{
  "filters": {
    "startDate": "",
    "endDate": ""
  }
}
```

The component tree will have me nest child components directly inside the parent tags, not as attributes as per Rule 7. I'll be using kebab-case for the element names. I'm using TypeScript, which has defined an HTML schema that I’ll be adhering to. Let's start sketching that out.
```html
<ui-column id="root">
   <ui-text id="titleText" text="# Company Dashboard" />
   <ui-card id="filtersCard">
      <ui-row id="filtersRow">
        <ui-date-time-input id="startDateInput" label="Start Date" value="{$/filters/startDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-date-time-input id="endDateInput" label="End Date" value="{$/filters/endDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-button id="applyBtn" on-click="{Event('apply_filters')}">
          <ui-text id="applyBtnText" text="Apply Filters" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>
   </ui-card>
   <ui-row id="metricsRow">
      <ui-card id="revenueCard" weight="{1}">
         <ui-column id="revenueCol">
            <ui-text id="revenueTitle" text="## Total Revenue" />
            <ui-text id="revenueValue" text="$1,234,567" />
         </ui-column>
      </ui-card>
      <ui-card id="usersCard" weight="{1}">
         <ui-column id="usersCol">
            <ui-text id="usersTitle" text="## New Users" />
            <ui-text id="usersValue" text="4,321" />
         </ui-column>
      </ui-card>
   </ui-row>
   <ui-card id="chartCard">
      <ui-column id="chartCol">
         <ui-text id="chartTitle" text="## Revenue Over Time" />
         <ui-image id="chartImage" url="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1551288049-bebda4e38f71?auto=format&fit=crop&w=1200&q=80" description="Line chart showing revenue over time" />
      </ui-column>
   </ui-card>
</ui-column>
```
Rule 7 is key here. It prevents a lot of layout misconfigurations that can happen when developers have an existing knowledge of React or Angular.

Now, let's double-check the components against HTML5 best practices and the A2UI rules. Prefixing all tags with `ui-`, unique `id`s, putting everything inside the parent tags (not as attributes), are crucial. All expressions are correctly wrapped in `{` and `}`, and data paths follow `{$/path}` format. For the `<ui-button>` I'll be using `on-click` to respond to the click event correctly, as the TypeScript definitions support an action to be used as an attribute.

I have double checked the attribute formatting and have ensured the HTML is now well-formed.

The image component will use a placeholder chart, like a screenshot of a line chart from an open resource. No need to overcomplicate the visual at this stage.

Finally, the code blocks will go inside a root `<body>`

The core structure will be a vertical column (`<ui-column>`) with `id="root"`—that's the root container. Inside, I’ll add a text heading, a filter section with date inputs and an apply button. Then two metrics cards in a row. Finally a card with a chart. I'll need a way to initialize those date values.

Data initialization is handled with a JSON script. I'll be initializing `startDate` and `endDate` to empty strings within the data model. This allows for clean handling of the filter data. The data model is:
```json
{
  "filters": {
    "startDate": "",
    "endDate": ""
  }
}
```

The component tree will have me nest child components directly inside the parent tags, not as attributes as per Rule 7. I'll be using kebab-case for the element names. I'm using TypeScript, which has defined an HTML schema that I’ll be adhering to. Let's start sketching that out.
```html
<ui-column id="root">
   <ui-text id="titleText" text="# Company Dashboard" />
   <ui-card id="filtersCard">
      <ui-row id="filtersRow">
        <ui-date-time-input id="startDateInput" label="Start Date" value="{$/filters/startDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-date-time-input id="endDateInput" label="End Date" value="{$/filters/endDate}" enable-date="{true}" />
        <ui-button id="applyBtn" on-click="{Event('apply_filters')}">

        </ui-button>

      </ui-column>
   </ui-card>
</ui-column>
```
Rule 7 is key here. It prevents a lot of layout misconfigurations that can happen when developers have an existing knowledge of React or Angular.

Prefixing all tags with `ui-`, unique `id`s, putting everything inside the parent tags (not as attributes), are crucial. For the `<ui-button>` I'll be using `on-click` to respond to the click event correctly, as the TypeScript definitions support an action to be used as an attribute.

I have double checked the attribute formatting and have ensured the HTML is now well-formed.

The image component will use a placeholder chart, like a screenshot of a line chart from an open resource. No need to overcomplicate the visual at this stage.

Finally, the code blocks will go inside a root `<body>`

The top-level element is a vertical `Column` with the ID `root`. Within that, I'll have a main title and a `List` to display the trip's three days. Each day is a `Card` containing the day's title and another `List` of activities. Each activity is presented as a `Row`, containing a `CheckBox` to mark completion, and a `Text` element for the description.

I've decided to structure it statically. This involves explicit IDs and nested components.  I need to make sure the structure matches "The first Card," "The second Card," "The third Card." I need to ensure the components are nested properly, *not* passed as attributes.

The data model is crucial. I'll initialize it using a `<script type="application/json">` tag, creating a data structure for storing the checkbox states for each activity: a set of boolean flags for each day/activity.

The final HTML structure will be enclosed within `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>` tags. The `body` element has `id="main"` and needs the `<link rel="catalog" ...>` tag at the start. It houses a text element with the title and a `List` with the day's cards. Each card contains a `Column` for the day's heading and a `List` for the activities, each represented by a `Row`. Particularly, I'm making sure I'm using the `label=""` correctly and mapping the `value` of the checkboxes to the correct data bindings and using the correct data paths. This static approach offers very explicit structure, which is a perfect fit for this rigid layout requirement. I've also verified that I'm nesting child components and not trying to pass properties as attributes on parent tags. All alignment and ID properties are correct and meet specifications. Okay, so the goal is to create a Kanban board UI for the "main" surface using A2UI.  I need to start with the top-level structure, which is a vertical `ui-column` acting as the root, with ID "root". Inside this, there will be a title using `ui-text`, and then the main layout which is a horizontal `ui-row` containing three vertical `ui-column`s for "To Do", "In Progress", and "Done".

I need to make sure I am nesting components correctly, as A2UI has specific rules. Specifically,  layout properties like `children` *must* be nested directly inside the parent tag, *not* as attributes. This is straightforward; I'll use standard HTML-style nesting.  I am thinking it is simpler and clearer to nest the individual `ui-card` elements directly inside each `ui-column` to visually represent the task list for each column.

Each `ui-column` will have a header using `ui-text`, and then the individual `ui-card` elements, each containing a `ui-text` element for the task title. I'll need to use unique IDs for every single component. I can see that markdown is supported in the headers using `ui-text`, so I'll format the column titles (like "## To Do") using markdown.

I need to make sure the three columns in the board layout take equal space. So, I will set `weight="{1}"` on each of the three `ui-column` components to ensure they are equally spaced.

I'll wrap the whole structure with the `<a2ui>` and `</body>` tags, including the catalog link at the start of the `<body>` element. I'll put the catalog link at the beginning, like the instructions say.  The surface ID is set with `<body>` id="main"`. **Kanban Board UI - A2UI Implementation**

Okay, so the goal is to create a Kanban board UI for the "main" surface using A2UI.  I need to start with the top-level structure, which is a vertical `ui-column` acting as the root, with ID "root". Inside this, there will be a title using `ui-text`, and then the main layout which is a horizontal `ui-row` containing three vertical `ui-column`s for "To Do", "In Progress", and "Done".

I need to make sure I am nesting components correctly, as A2UI has specific rules. Specifically,  layout properties like `children` *must* be nested directly inside the parent tag, *not* as attributes. This is straightforward; I'll use standard HTML-style nesting.  I am thinking it is simpler and clearer to nest the individual `ui-card` elements directly inside each `ui-column` to visually represent the task list for each column.

Each `ui-column` will have a header using `ui-text`, and then the individual `ui-card` elements, each containing a `ui-text` element for the task title. I'll need to use unique IDs for every single component. I can see that markdown is supported in the headers using `ui-text`, so I'll format the column titles (like "## To Do") using markdown.

I need to make sure the three columns in the board layout take equal space. So, I will set `weight="{1}"` on each of the three `ui-column` components to ensure they are equally spaced.

I'll wrap the whole structure with the `<a2ui>` and `</body>` tags, including the catalog link at the start of the `<body>` element. I'll put the catalog link at the beginning, like the instructions say.  The surface ID is set with `<body>` id="main"`. Finally, I'll go through and do a final check to verify everything has a unique ID and is structured according to the rules. No dynamic data binding is needed here as this a fixed Kanban structure.

output.completion:
<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <ui-column id="root">
      <ui-text id="boardTitle" text="# Project Tasks" />
      <ui-row id="kanbanRow">
        
        <!-- To Do Column -->
        <ui-column id="todoColumn" weight="{1}">
          <ui-text id="todoHeader" text="## To Do" />
          <ui-card id="cardResearch">
            <ui-text id="txtResearch" text="Research" />
          </ui-card>
          <ui-card id="cardDesign">
            <ui-text id="txtDesign" text="Design" />
          </ui-card>
        </ui-column>

        <!-- In Progress Column -->
        <ui-column id="inProgressColumn" weight="{1}">
          <ui-text id="inProgressHeader" text="## In Progress" />
          <ui-card id="cardImplementation">
            <ui-text id="txtImplementation" text="Implementation" />
          </ui-card>
        </ui-column>

        <!-- Done Column -->
        <ui-column id="doneColumn" weight="{1}">
          <ui-text id="doneHeader" text="## Done" />
          <ui-card id="cardPlanning">
            <ui-text id="txtPlanning" text="Planning" />
          </ui-card>
        </ui-column>

      </ui-row>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

**My Thinking Process for Building the Video Call Interface**

Okay, so the task is to craft an A2UI markup for a video call interface. Let's break this down systematically.

First, I need to understand the requirements. The core components are a text header, a video player with a placeholder URL, and a row of three buttons: Mute, Camera, and End Call. It's A2UI, so I need to adhere to the framework's specific HTML5-like format, including kebab-case for attributes and proper nesting. Unique IDs are essential. The overall structure needs to be within `<a2ui>` and `</body>`.

Next, I'll define the component hierarchy. A `ui-column` will be the root, labeled "root", and I will need to nest inside it, `ui-text`, `ui-video`, and a `ui-row`. The row will contain the three `ui-button` components, each with its corresponding `ui-text`. I'll use a valid placeholder video URL.

**My File Browser UI - A2UI Implementation**

Okay, so the goal is to build a file browser UI using the A2UI framework. Let's break this down systematically. First, I need to visualize the structure: a title, followed by a list of file entries. The title will be a simple text element, styled as a header. The file entries will be rows within a list, each row containing an icon and the filename as text.

I'm thinking, based on the prompt, it needs to be strictly A2UI. Therefore, I'll need to use A2UI elements, rules, and schema, and I'll need to double check the specification for how those elements work.

Now, let's get into the specifics. I will use a `ui-column` as the root component to wrap everything: title and list. The title will be a `ui-text` component with the text "# My Files". The list of file entries needs to be implemented using `<ui-list>`. Since this is a static list (not data-bound), I can't use `<template>`. So, the `<ui-row>` elements will be nested directly within the `<ui-list>`.

Each row will contain an `ui-icon` and a `ui-text`. The `ui-icon` will have a `name` attribute which can be either "folder" or "attachFile". The `ui-text` component will contain the filename.

I should also make sure to assign unique `id` attributes to each component for easy referencing. So the structure will look something like this:

```html
<ui-column id="root">
  <ui-text id="title" text="# My Files" />
  <ui-list id="fileList">
    <ui-row id="rowDocuments">
      <ui-icon id="iconDocuments" name="folder" />
      <ui-text id="textDocuments" text="Documents" />
    </ui-row>
    ... more rows ...
  </ui-list>
</ui-column>
```

Alright, properties: `ui-text` needs `id` and `text`. `ui-icon` needs `id` and `name`. `ui-row` should also have an `id`, and maybe attributes to control layout like `justify` or `align`. Also, for the `ui-list`, I will need to set the `id` and probably set the `direction` attribute to "vertical".

The example entries I need: "Documents" (folder icon), "Images" (folder icon), and "Work.txt" (attachFile icon).

Let's do a quick layout check: `ui-column` at the root, then a `ui-text` for the title, and then a `ui-list`. The list contains `ui-row` components and each `ui-row` has an `ui-icon` and a `ui-text`.

I will need to ensure that the component tags use the `ui-` prefix, all elements have unique `id` attributes, and there is no unnecessary dynamic logic since this is a static layout.

I should include the catalog link in the `<body id="main">` element like: `<link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">`.

So, the markup, after careful consideration, should look like:

```html
<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <ui-column id="root" align="start">
      <ui-text id="title" text="# My Files" />
      <ui-list id="fileList" direction="vertical" align="stretch">
        <ui-row id="rowDocuments" align="center">
          <ui-icon id="iconDocuments" name="folder" />
          <ui-text id="textDocuments" text="Documents" />
        </ui-row>
        <ui-row id="rowImages" align="center">
          <ui-icon id="iconImages" name="folder" />

        </ui-row>
        <ui-row id="rowWork" align="center">
          <ui-icon id="iconWork" name="attachFile" />
          <ui-text id="textWork" text="Work.txt" />
        </ui-row>
      </ui-list>
    </ui-column>

<ui-column id="root">

I immediately start by reviewing the API documentation, carefully checking each component's usage. The root element *must* have the ID "root." The message history needs `Card` components for each message, and each `Card` needs to contain the message content, so I can nest a layout component (like a `Column` or a `Row`) inside the card for the content. I remember the rule about not defining the child component inline for the Card, and that the child needs to be nested directly inside the parent tag, *not* as an attribute.

I need a way to represent the messages, and quickly decide on a dynamic list using a JSON data structure. Using the provided messages ("Alice: Hi there!", "Bob: Hello!") is essential, so I'll initialize them within the JSON data. The `<ui-list>` component and a `<template>` tag seem ideal for creating this dynamic list. I remember to *not* duplicate the template's child components anywhere else in the document as the guidelines say. I then move to the overall layout. A root `Column` will be the foundation. Within that, I'll need a message history *Column* (or the `ui-list`) that will contain message *Card* components. Each card will contain a `Column` for the sender and message body. The *bottom* will contain the *input row*, which has a `TextField` for the message and a `Button` to send it.

The Button's `child` is an A2UIElement, so I can nest a `<ui-text>` directly inside the button. I recall the guidelines regarding nesting components.

I plan for a `Column` for the message history and set `weight="{1}"` so it can expand to fill the available vertical space. I need the input row to be at the bottom, so I'll set `justify="spaceBetween"` on the root `Column` or `justify="start"` on the history `Column` which gives the same visual result. For the input row's TextField, I can set `weight="{1}"` to take up most of the horizontal space, and for styling, I'll use the `variant` property on the sender's text component, like `variant="caption"`. I can also use `variant="primary"` on the send button. I'll add a header for the chat room too.

I make sure to follow the kebab-case convention for component names (ui-column, ui-card, etc.), ensure unique IDs for all components, and double-check my use of curly braces for bindings and weights (`{$/newMessage}`, `weight="{1}"`). <a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "newMessage": ""
      }
    </script>

    <ui-column id="root" justify="spaceBetween" align="stretch">
      <!-- Message history column -->
      <ui-column id="historyColumn" justify="start" align="stretch" weight="{1}">
        
        <!-- Message 1 -->
        <ui-card id="messageCard1">
          <ui-column id="messageLayout1" align="start">
            <ui-text id="sender1" text="Alice" variant="caption" />
            <ui-text id="body1" text="Hi there!" variant="body" />

        </ui-card>

        <!-- Message 2 -->
        <ui-card id="messageCard2">
          <ui-column id="messageLayout2" align="start">
            <ui-text id="sender2" text="Bob" variant="caption" />
            <ui-text id="body2" text="Hello!" variant="body" />
          </ui-column>
        </ui-card>

      </ui-column>

      <ui-divider id="divider" axis="horizontal" />

      <!-- Input controls area at the bottom -->
      <ui-row id="inputRow" justify="spaceBetween" align="center">
        <ui-text-field id="messageInput" label="Type a message..." value="{$/newMessage}" weight="{1}" />
        <ui-button id="sendButton" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('send_message')}">
          <ui-text id="sendButtonText" text="Send" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

Inside, include several 'Card's representing messages, each with a 'Text' for the sender and a 'Text' for the message body. Specifically include these messages: "Alice: Hi there!", "Bob: Hello!". At the bottom, a 'Row' with a 'TextField' (label "Type a message...") and a 'Button' labeled "Send".

content.summary:
**Chat Room Interface Construction: A Detailed Plan**

Okay, so I need to build a chat room UI. First, the goal is clear: a message history display, an input field, and a "Send" button. The structure should include a message history column and then, at the bottom, an input row with a text field and a button.

I immediately start by reviewing the API documentation, carefully checking each component's usage. The root element *must* have the ID "root." The message history needs `Card` components for each message, and each `Card` needs to contain the message content, so I can nest a layout component (like a `Column` or a `Row`) inside the card for the content. I remember the rule about not defining the child component inline for the Card, and that the child needs to be nested directly inside the parent tag, *not* as an attribute.

I need a way to represent the messages, and quickly decide on a dynamic list using a JSON data structure. Using the provided messages ("Alice: Hi there!", "Bob: Hello!") is essential, so I'll initialize them within the JSON data. The `<ui-list>` component and a `<template>` tag seem ideal for creating this dynamic list. I remember to *not* duplicate the template's child components anywhere else in the document as the guidelines say. However, the requirement is so literal ("Specifically include these messages") that it might be safest to just render static `Card` elements for those two messages, but I will make the dynamic solution too.

I then move to the overall layout. A root `Column` will be the foundation. Within that, I'll need a message history *Column* (or the `ui-list`) that will contain message *Card* components. Each card will contain a `Column` for the sender and message body. The *bottom* will contain the *input row*, which has a `TextField` for the message and a `Button` to send it.

The Button's `child` is an A2UIElement, so I can nest a `<ui-text>` directly inside the button. I recall the guidelines regarding nesting components.

I plan for a `Column` for the message history and set `weight="{1}"` so it can expand to fill the available vertical space. I need the input row to be at the bottom, so I'll set `justify="spaceBetween"` on the root `Column` or `justify="start"` on the history `Column` which gives the same visual result. For the input row's TextField, I can set `weight="{1}"` to take up most of the horizontal space, and for styling, I'll use the `variant` property on the sender's text component, like `variant="caption"`. I can also use `variant="primary"` on the send button. I'll add a header for the chat room too.

I make sure to follow the kebab-case convention for component names (ui-column, ui-card, etc.), ensure unique IDs for all components, and double-check my use of curly braces for bindings and weights (`{$/newMessage}`, `weight="{1}"`). Event actions, like the `send_message`, will be properly defined using `on-click="{Event('send_message')}"`. I must specify that components are nested directly without using layout properties as attributes. The catalog link is also crucial. The structure of the `Card` component is also thoroughly re-checked, with a nested `Column`. I plan to use a Divider to organize the layout.

Before I finalize, I review everything: the specific messages are included, the bottom row with the text field and button is there. Component spellings are right, events and bindings are correct, weights are used correctly, no layout attributes where they don't belong, catalog link exists, root ID and body ID are present. It's clean, robust, and fulfills all requirements in a very elegant, complete manner. I am now confident about the output and will render it.

output.completion:
<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "newMessage": ""
      }
    </script>

    <ui-column id="root" justify="spaceBetween" align="stretch">
      <!-- Message history column -->
      <ui-column id="historyColumn" justify="start" align="stretch" weight="{1}">
        
        <!-- Message 1 -->
        <ui-card id="messageCard1">
          <ui-column id="messageLayout1" align="start">
            <ui-text id="sender1" text="Alice" variant="caption" />
            <ui-text id="body1" text="Hi there!" variant="body" />
          </ui-column>
        </ui-card>

        <!-- Message 2 -->
        <ui-card id="messageCard2">
          <ui-column id="messageLayout2" align="start">
            <ui-text id="sender2" text="Bob" variant="caption" />
            <ui-text id="body2" text="Hello!" variant="body" />
          </ui-column>
        </ui-card>

      </ui-column>

      <ui-divider id="divider" axis="horizontal" />

      <!-- Input controls area at the bottom -->
      <ui-row id="inputRow" justify="spaceBetween" align="center">
        <ui-text-field id="messageInput" label="Type a message..." value="{$/newMessage}" weight="{1}" />
        <ui-button id="sendButton" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('send_message')}">
          <ui-text id="sendButtonText" text="Send" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

Okay, let's break this down. I need to grade this submitted JSON payload against a very specific A2UI criterion. The goal is to see if it's a valid "main" surface, and the structure has a root column, a message history column with two chat cards, and an input row.

First, I see the surface ID matches 'main', so that's a check. The root component is indeed a column with the correct children as defined. Looking deeper at the message history column, it contains the correct cards.

Now, let's examine the chat card contents. I see Alice's message, which should be "Alice: Hi there!", but it's just "Alice". The criterion asks for "Alice:" with the colon, but the submitted version is missing it. Same with Bob, the criterion requires "Bob:" but the submission shows just "Bob."

Is that a critical failure? Let's consult the rules. Rule 1 says punctuation variations are acceptable if the semantic intent is there. Rule 7 allows for partial credit for minor cosmetic differences. However, Rule 1 says acceptable, which implies "fully correct", not partial.

I look at the task requirements. The submission has "Alice" and "Hi there!" inside a message layout, which structurally and semantically represents "Alice: Hi there!". The sender and body are correctly separated as expected for a chat card.

Is anything else missing? No. The structure is spot-on. I'm going to lean towards grading this as correct. The missing colon is a minor punctuation detail, and that's covered by Note 1.

Let's do a quick verification.
- Valid "root" Column for history and input? Yes.
- Message history Column with two cards? Yes.
- One card with "Alice:" (or "Alice") and "Hi there!"? Yes.
- The other card with "Bob:" (or "Bob") and "Hello!"? Yes.
- Input Row has the TextField and Button? Yes.

Everything checks out. The submission matches the A2UI spec v1.0.

Therefore, the grade is C.

**Smart Home Dashboard - A2UI Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down. My goal is to craft a smart home dashboard using A2UI Elemental markup, focusing on a clear, well-structured UI that showcases the data bindings. The task requires a `Column` as the root element and nested `Row`s and `Card`s.

First, I need to ensure a valid A2UI structure. The root element must have `id="root"`, and all data binding uses the `{$/path}` format. I will initialize the data as specified in the prompt: `lightsState` to `true`, `thermostatValue` to `72`, and `musicState` to `false`.

Now, I understand the crucial aspect here is the nesting structure: I *must* nest child components directly inside their parent tags, no exceptions. The rules state that I should *not* pass layout properties like `children` or `child` as attributes and *must* use nested syntax. This is confirmed by checking Example 2, where the `<ui-list>` element is nested inside a `<ui-card>` element.

Let's begin the layout. I'll declare the root as a `Column` (id="root"). It will contain a `Text` element with `id="header"` and text `"# Living Room"`. Then, for the grid, I will define two `Row` components (id="row1" and id="row2"), nested directly inside the root `Column`.

Within each row, I'll place the `Card` components. Inside `row1`, there will be two `Card`s: "Lights" and "Thermostat." The "Lights" card will contain a `CheckBox` (id="lightsCheckbox"), and the "Thermostat" card will have a `Slider` (id="thermostatSlider"). In `row2`, a "Music" `Card` will include a `CheckBox` (id="musicCheckbox"). I'll bind the data to each of these elements.

For styling, I'll ensure alignment where needed and add the `weight` property to each of the cards in a row.

I'll double-check to make sure I've wrapped numbers, booleans, and expressions in double-quoted curly braces (e.g., `max="{100}"`), and I've constructed the UI on surfaceId 'main'. Also, there should be a catalog link in the body, and the entire block should be wrapped within `<a2ui>` tags.

Let's finalize the code.

    </ui-row>
  </ui-column>
</body>
</a2ui>

**Menu Markup Mastery: A Deep Dive into A2UI Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. My goal is to craft a restaurant menu using A2UI's elemental HTML5-like markup, ensuring adherence to the specified structure and best practices. First, I need to truly grasp the requirements: a title, a tabbed interface ("Starters," "Mains," "Desserts"), and the content within each tab presented as a list of rows, each row detailing a menu item's name and price.

The initial challenge is the component hierarchy and the ID referencing convention within the A2UI framework. I need to be absolutely sure of how children are defined, particularly regarding the use of IDs. Based on my review, I understand that children are *not* defined inline as attributes but are *nested* directly within the parent tags, and are *referenced* by their IDs. The `ui-tabs` component uses a special `tabs` attribute. Rule 5 guides me here: I should use a JSON literal within a `<script type="application/json" slot="tabs">` tag to define the tab configuration, instead of trying to pass it as a regular attribute. This seems much cleaner.

So, I need to create the JSON that defines the tabs and their associated content, referencing the IDs of the child components that hold the actual menu items. Inside the tabs, I'll need `ui-list` components, which in turn contain `ui-row` components. Within each `ui-row`, I'll place `ui-text` components for the item name and price. I also need to use the `justify` attribute of ui-row to space the name and price nicely.

Next, I need to define the structure meticulously. The root will be a `ui-column`, the header will be a `ui-text`, and the tab container will be a `ui-tabs`. Then, inside `ui-tabs`, I'll nest a `<script>` tag with the JSON configuration, and then the menu content components.

Let's carefully create the JSON object, mapping tab titles to their corresponding `ui-list` IDs. The menu layout will follow a simple but clear structure with a main column for the overall layout. The text elements and tab labels should be clear. I must ensure all components have unique IDs, following a consistent naming scheme (`headerText`, `menuTabs`, `startersList`, etc.). The items need to look nice and organized. I will use `justify="spaceBetween"` to separate the name and price in each row.

Now, let's meticulously assemble the markup: I'll nest each component correctly within its parent, making sure the `tabs` JSON is correctly placed within its slot. I'll define all menu items with correct `id` and `text` attributes, and ensure each component adheres to the A2UI syntax.

Finally, I'll perform a final sanity check, ensuring all rules are respected: that the markup is valid, properly nested, and utilizes IDs correctly. I'll make sure there are no syntax errors and that the structure exactly mirrors the requirements, especially the static tab definition via the JSON slot. I'll use the A2UI sentinel tags. Excellent, everything looks shipshape.

<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">{}</script>
    <ui-column id="root" align="stretch">
      <ui-text id="headerText" text="# Gourmet Bistro" />
      <ui-tabs id="menuTabs">
        <script type="application/json" slot="tabs">
          [
            {
              "title": "Starters",
              "child": "startersList"
            },
            {
              "title": "Mains",
              "child": "mainsList"
            },
            {
              "title": "Desserts",
              "child": "dessertsList"
            }
          ]
        </script>
        
        <ui-list id="startersList" direction="vertical">
          <ui-row id="starterRow1" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="starter1Name" text="Soup" />
            <ui-text id="starter1Price" text="$8" />
          </ui-row>
          <ui-row id="starterRow2" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="starter2Name" text="Salad" />
            <ui-text id="starter2Price" text="$10" />
          </ui-row>
        </ui-list>

        <ui-list id="mainsList" direction="vertical">
          <ui-row id="mainRow1" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="main1Name" text="Steak" />
            <ui-text id="main1Price" text="$25" />
          </ui-row>
          <ui-row id="mainRow2" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="main2Name" text="Pasta" />
            <ui-text id="main2Price" text="$18" />
          </ui-row>
        </ui-list>

        <ui-list id="dessertsList" direction="vertical">
          <ui-row id="dessertRow1" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="dessert1Name" text="Cake" />
            <ui-text id="dessert1Price" text="$8" />
          </ui-row>
          <ui-row id="dessertRow2" justify="spaceBetween">
            <ui-text id="dessert2Name" text="Pie" />
            <ui-text id="dessert2Price" text="$7" />
          </ui-row>
        </ui-list>
      </ui-tabs>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

            </ui-button>
          </ui-column>
        </ui-card>

        <ui-card id="sportsCard">
          <ui-column id="sportsCol" align="start">
            <ui-image id="sportsImg" url="https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1461896836934-ffe607ba8211?w=600" description="Local athletes on a running track" variant="mediumFeature" />
            <ui-text id="sportsTitle" text="Local Sports" />
            <ui-text id="sportsDesc" text="The hometown team clinched a dramatic last-second victory last night, securing their spot in the regional championship tournament." />
            <ui-button id="sportsBtn" on-click="{openUrl(url: 'https://example.com/sports')}" variant="primary">
              <ui-text id="sportsBtnLabel" text="Read More" />
            </ui-button>
          </ui-column>
        </ui-card>
      </ui-list>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

content.summary:
**Photo Editor Interface - Design Process**

Okay, so I'm tasked with creating a photo editor UI. My first thought is, let's break this down systematically. The core components are a large image, a row of buttons, and an intensity slider. The key, as I read it, is to start with the fundamental structure and then nest the components properly to avoid inline definitions.

The initial layout is pretty straightforward: a column, which I'll call `ui-column`, as the root to stack elements. Inside, a large image (`ui-image`). I need to make the image large; the spec says to use `variant="largeFeature"`, and I'll need a `url` attribute for the photo, binding it to a URL within a JSON data section. Then, a row (`ui-row`) for the buttons – "Filters", "Crop", and "Adjust". Each button needs a label. That implies `ui-button` components, and I have to use nested `ui-text` elements within each `ui-button` for the labels, not inline. That is key: the `child` property on the button refers to the ID of the text, so I will nest directly! The slider (`ui-slider`) is next. I'll need to set the `label` to "Intensity", and the min and max and default value. Since they are numerical properties, I need to enclose the numeric properties in double-quoted curly braces.

I need to make sure I am using event handlers too. I need to make sure I implement button click event handlers using `on-click`, and event handling by wrapping the event with the `Event` function. So each `ui-button` will have an `on-click` attribute that calls an `Event` function.

Now, let's get the data loaded. I can't forget the JSON at the root of the page to initialize the image URL and the slider value. I need a `<script type="application/json">` tag, and I will define a `photoUrl` and `intensity` property in JSON. I'll use the JSON binding for the slider's `value` attribute, too.

Looking back at the requirements, I must prefix every component with `ui-`. Unique IDs for everything are a must. No dynamic styling. Numbers, booleans, and expressions need the double curly braces. The whole thing has to be wrapped in `<a2ui>` tags, and the catalog link needs to be in the `<body>`. The key is remembering to nest the `ui-text` inside the `ui-button`, even though the Button TS interface suggests otherwise.

Okay, let's build the HTML. First, the `<a2ui>` tag. I'll start with the data initialization using JSON and then construct the layout, top to bottom. I will add basic event handlers that can be replaced later.

Time for a final review. I'll check my IDs, ensure the large image is there, the row of buttons, the slider, the data binding, event attributes, nested children, the catalog link, and that all numeric values and bindings are in the right format. Looks like I've covered everything. Ready to roll!

<a2ui>
  <body id="main">
    <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "photoUrl": "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1579783900882-c0d3dad7b119?w=800&auto=format&fit=crop",
        "intensity": 50
      }
    </script>
    <ui-column id="root" justify="start" align="stretch">
      <!-- Large Image Photo Preview -->
      <ui-image id="editorImage" url="{$/photoUrl}" description="Photo Editor Preview" variant="largeFeature" fit="contain" />

      <!-- Row of Edit Actions -->
      <ui-row id="editorActionsRow" justify="spaceEvenly" align="center">
        <ui-button id="btnFilters" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('select_filters')}">
          <ui-text id="txtFilters" text="Filters" />
        </ui-button>
        
        <ui-button id="btnCrop" variant="default" on-click="{Event('select_crop')}">
          <ui-text id="txtCrop" text="Crop" />
        </ui-button>
        
        <ui-button id="btnAdjust" variant="default" on-click="{Event('select_adjust')}">
          <ui-text id="txtAdjust" text="Adjust" />
        </ui-button>
      </ui-row>

      <!-- Intensity Control Slider -->
      <ui-slider id="intensitySlider" label="Intensity" min="{0}" max="{100}" value="{$/intensity}" />
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

content.summary:
**Quiz UI Component Creation: A Step-by-Step Breakdown**

Okay, let's get this done. The goal is clear: build a UI for a trivia quiz question, complete with specific components.  First, the essentials: text for the question and header, a choice picker for answers, and a submit button.  I'll start by defining the structure, a stacked layout, and the elements needed.  The root will be a `ui-column`, perfect for vertical stacking, with each UI element nested inside in order: header text, question text, a choice picker, and the submit button.

Next, I'll think about the data. We'll need a state variable, let's call it `/selectedAnswer`, and initialize it as an empty array in the data.  Now, the `ChoicePicker`. It'll be mutually exclusive for single-answer questions, and will need a value binding to `/selectedAnswer`, and an options script. Let's define the attributes: `id` is `answerPicker`, `variant` is `mutuallyExclusive`, and `value` is bound to the state variable.  The options are defined using a JSON slot, with labels and values.

The `Button` needs a child component, the UI definition says: "Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button." and rule 7 says to nest the child directly.  So the  `Button`'s child is `ui-text`.  Let's create it. The button's event handler will trigger an `Event` function with `submit_answer`.

Okay, let's refine those IDs for clarity: The main layout will be `root`, the header is `qHeader`, the question is `qText`, the choice picker is `answerPicker`, the button is `submitBtn` and the button text is `submitBtnText`.

I need to validate, of course.  I'll ensure I am following the rules: the root element has the correct id, elements are prefixed with `ui-`, expressions wrapped in double curly braces, and functions called with named arguments.  The `value` property of the `ChoicePicker` needs to be an array of strings, so that is correct.

Now, let's craft the XML structure. It'll be a standard A2UI structure with the appropriate catalog link.  The body will contain the data initialization and the stacked column of components. I'll bind the data, use the `ui-choice-picker`, use a json slot for the options. The button event calls an `Event` function with the `/selectedAnswer` data.

Finally, I'll double-check the layout. Rule 7 is clear, nesting components directly within the column is the way to go. There is no need for explicit `children` or `child` attributes.  And, for good measure, I'll add a touch of visual spacing where possible.  I'll make sure to double check that `variant` is supported on the choice picker. <a2ui>
  <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json" />
  <body id="main">
    <script type="application/json">
      {
        "selectedAnswer": []
      }
    </script>
    <ui-column id="root" justify="start" align="stretch">
      <ui-text id="questionNumber" text="# Question 1" />
      <ui-text id="questionText" text="What is the capital of France?" />
      <ui-choice-picker id="answerPicker" variant="mutuallyExclusive" value="{$/selectedAnswer}">
        <script type="application/json" slot="options">
          [
            {"label": "Paris", "value": "Paris"},
            {"label": "London", "value": "London"},
            {"label": "Berlin", "value": "Berlin"},
            {"label": "Madrid", "value": "Madrid"}
          ]
        </script>
      </ui-choice-picker>
      <ui-button id="submitButton" variant="primary" on-click="{Event('submitAnswer', {answer: $/selectedAnswer})}">
        <ui-text id="submitButtonText" text="Submit Answer" />
      </ui-button>
    </ui-column>
  </body>
</a2ui>

content.summary:
**Calculator UI Implementation Plan**

Alright, let's break down this calculator UI request. First, the goal is to create a calculator interface on the 'main' surface. We need a root component with `id="root"`, and a `<ui-card>` seems like the best choice. This card will contain a single `Column` for layout.

Inside this column, we'll nest two key components: a `Text` element displaying "0" (initially), and another `Column` to hold all the calculator buttons arranged in rows and columns. This display will be static. I will use a simple string as requested, so the content of `ui-text` will be `text="0"`. No need for data bindings at this stage.

Now, for the nested `Column` containing the buttons, we'll set up four `Row` components. Each row holds a specific set of buttons: "7", "8", "9", "/", then "4", "5", "6", "*", then "1", "2", "3", "-", and finally "0", ".", "=", "+". Each of these buttons will be a `<ui-button>` with an embedded `<ui-text>` component for their respective labels.

The primary directive is strict adherence to the A2UI component structure. That means adhering to the nesting rules: no attributes for child components - they must be nested directly within their parent tags. The layout is a straightforward nested `Column`/`Row` structure inside the `<ui-card>`.

Looking at the A2UI component interfaces, a `<ui-card>` only supports a single `child` component, and it must be nested. `<ui-column>` supports the same nesting. For the buttons, `<ui-button>` similarly uses nesting for the button label's text.

The button actions need to be handled with `on-click`. So, for each button click, the system needs to send an event. I will make a generic `press` event, with key values, such as  `on-click="{Event('press', {value: '7'})}"`. I am keeping it simple and using an `Event()` call. I will use named arguments to be extremely clean. Alternatively, a simpler `on-click="{Event('button_7')}"` avoids parsing issues. It looks like `Event('press', {value: '7'})` is perfectly correct since its an expression.

Let's make sure that IDs are unique (kebab-case), all child components are nested, and all the styling helpers are appropriate. Finally, the display's text will show "0" initially. We're keeping it a static value, in order to comply with the instructions exactly. With these rules in place, we're ready to define the XML/HTML structure.

  <link rel="catalog" href="https://a2ui.org/specification/v1_0/catalogs/basic/catalog.json" />
  <body id="main">
    <ui-card id="root">
      <ui-column id="calculator-column" justify="start" align="stretch">
        
        <!-- Display showing "0" -->
        <ui-text id="display-text" text="0" />
        
        <!-- Nested Column of Rows for Buttons -->
        <ui-column id="buttons-container" justify="start" align="stretch">
          
          <!-- Row 1: "7", "8", "9", "/" -->
          <ui-row id="row-1" justify="spaceEvenly" align="center">
            <ui-button id="btn-7" on-click="{Event('key_press_7')}">
              <ui-text id="lbl-7" text="7" />
            </ui-button>
            <ui-button id="btn-8" on-click="{Event('key_press_8')}">
              <ui-text id="lbl-8" text="8" />
            </ui-button>
